builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted assistant is too expensive because its model uses most of the GPU memory.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's supported lower-precision weights on a copy of your serving setup.
builder_plan.baseline: The same model at its original precision, on the same GPU.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Peak memory, task pass rate, latency, and total serving cost at the same context and load.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Balancing hierarchical representation and quantization: A performance trade-off in text embeddings
summary: This replaces storing full-precision, full-dimensionality embedding vectors (float32 at native dimension) with int8-quantized, dimensionally truncated hierarchical embeddings. The cost is at most roughly 1.5 percentage points of effectiveness overall and a small integration effort to emit and store shorter quantized vectors, with no measured evaluation speedup from quantization itself. It can fail on retrieval tasks, which degrade far faster than other categories, and binary quantization or two successive dimension halvings are significantly worse and should not be adopted.
rationale: The 32x storage saving directly lowers vector-database memory and cloud cost on constrained infrastructure with statistically negligible quality loss for non-retrieval tasks, provided retrieval workloads are validated separately.
technique: Hierarchical dimensionality reduction with int8 embedding quantization

claims.statement: This replaces storing full-precision, full-dimensionality embedding vectors (float32 at native dimension) with int8-quantized, dimensionally truncated hierarchical embeddings. The cost is at most roughly 1.5 percentage points of effectiveness overall and a small integration effort to emit and store shorter quantized vectors, with no measured evaluation speedup from quantization itself. It can fail on retrieval tasks, which degrade far faster than other categories, and binary quantization or two successive dimension halvings are significantly worse and should not be adopted.

Combining 8x dimensionality reduction with int8 quantization reduces per-vector storage 32x while retaining 94.4% of baseline effectiveness; int8 alone is statistically indistinguishable from float32 for pair classification and re-ranking and costs at most 1.5 percentage points overall.
